browser.definizione: The program you use to visit websites, such as Chrome, Safari, Firefox or Edge.

archiviazione-locale.definizione: A small space the browser reserves for each website to save data on your device. The data stays only in that browser and on that device.

cloud.definizione: Real computers, sitting in a company's data centers, that you use over the internet without having them physically in front of you.

github.definizione: A website where people who develop software keep, share and work on their projects, including together with others.

codespaces.definizione: A GitHub service that gives you, in a few seconds, a ready-made computer in the cloud to use inside your browser.

hardware.definizione: The physical part of a computer: everything you can touch, such as processor, memory, disk, screen and keyboard.

software.definizione: The set of instructions that tell the hardware what to do: programs, apps, operating systems.

processore.definizione: The component that executes programs' instructions. It can have several cores working in parallel.

memoria-ram.definizione: The fast memory where the computer keeps the data it is working on right now. It empties when the computer turns off.

disco.definizione: The component that keeps data and programs even when the computer is off. Today it's usually an SSD, an electronic memory.

sistema-operativo.definizione: The software that manages the hardware and makes it available to other programs in an orderly and safe way, such as Linux, Windows or macOS.

kernel.definizione: The heart of the operating system: it talks directly to the hardware, and every program has to go through it to use processor, memory and disk.

linux.definizione: A free Unix-style kernel; by extension, the operating system built around it. It's the system containers were born on.

distribuzione.definizione: A complete operating system based on the Linux kernel, with its own programs and settings, such as Ubuntu or Debian.

programma.definizione: A set of instructions saved on the disk, ready to be executed.

processo.definizione: A running program: it uses processor and memory, it starts when you launch it and ends when it finishes or you close it.

pid.definizione: Process IDentifier: the unique number the kernel assigns to each process to recognize it.

file.definizione: A set of data saved on the disk with a name, such as a photo, a document or a program.

cartella.definizione: A container for files and other folders, used to keep them tidy.

file-system.definizione: The way the operating system organizes files and folders. On Linux it's a tree that starts from the root /.

applicazione.definizione: A program, or a set of programs, designed to do a job for people.

libreria.definizione: A set of already-written functions that programs can use instead of rewriting them from scratch.

dipendenza.definizione: A library or program an application needs in order to work, often in a precise version.

versione.definizione: The number that identifies a published state of a piece of software, for example 2.4.1 (major.minor.patch).
